## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

SensorReadingsSource.registerOne — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/reading/SensorReadingsSource.kt:87-110

## Trigger

register() calling registerOne() in sequence for each requested SensorDataType, itself called from ExerciseSessionManager.open() (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/session/ExerciseSessionManager.kt:88), itself called from RaceLaunchController.openPreparation() (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceLaunchController.kt:43), itself called from PreparationViewModel's init block (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/preparation/PreparationViewModel.kt:64) — observed

## Today

registerOne() wraps registerMeasureCallback in a suspendCancellableCoroutine that resumes only from the MeasureCallback's onRegistered or onRegistrationFailed. Neither callback carries a timeout: if the platform never calls either — the documented case of a data type this client cannot measure — the coroutine never resumes. register() (SensorReadingsSource.kt:57-65) calls registerOne() in a plain sequential loop with no timeout of its own, so one silent type blocks every type after it and the whole function. Nothing in the module bounds this wait; no withTimeoutOrNull or equivalent wraps the suspendCancellableCoroutine.

The same unbounded-wait shape exists in two other places identified in the same audit, both reachable ahead of this one in the wear preparation flow: SensorPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission() (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/permission/SensorPermissionSystemImpl.kt:84-91) and ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission() (core-platform/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/platform/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.kt:54-59). Each creates a CompletableDeferred, launches a system permission dialog, and awaits the deferred with no timeout; the deferred is completed only by onPermissionResult(), called from the launcher's callback. If the hosting activity is destroyed before that callback fires — the documented case — the deferred is never completed and the awaiting coroutine suspends for the remainder of the process's life.

## Expected

registerOne()'s suspendCancellableCoroutine is bounded by a timeout. On timeout, the registration for that data type is treated as a failure exactly like onRegistrationFailed: the type is not added to activeTypes/activeCallbacks, register()'s loop continues with the remaining types instead of hanging, and the timeout is logged as the failure reason.

SensorPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission() and ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission() each bound their deferred.await() with the same discipline: on timeout, requestPermission() returns false (a declined permission) instead of leaving the coroutine suspended indefinitely, and pendingResult is cleared so a callback arriving after the timeout does not resolve a deferred nobody still awaits.
